items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Researchers continue to explore the origins of the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, which weighs approximately six tonnes. A new international team's research found no matching source from the Scottish locations they examined, narrowing possibilities down. Previous assumptions about the Altar Stone's Welsh origins have been challenged by new geological insights.

items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A Louisiana woman accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of her late mother's estate to himself and businesses linked to him. More than 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived her claims concerning his handling of the estate but upheld the dismissal of other claims. It also cancelled a $10,000 damages award and ordered further proceedings.

items.title: 280 Ice Age engravings found in Spanish cave overlooked for 60 years
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: A remarkable archaeological find at Cova de la Font Major has revealed 280 Palaeolithic engravings, showcasing diverse motifs of animals and geometric shapes. This challenges the previously held notion that cave art was scarce in northeastern Iberia, where only two pieces were known. These engravings suggest the existence of unique artistic traditions independent of the famous Franco-Cantabrian region, offering new insights into the cultural practices of Ice Age Europe.

items.title: Black grouse chicks hatch in North York Moors after nearly 200-year absence
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a remarkable conservation achievement, black grouse have successfully hatched chicks in North York Moors after a long absence of 200 years. In 2024, 20 black grouse were moved from North Pennines as part of a dedicated effort that includes habitat restoration and management of predators. Reports indicate a notable rise in the number of displaying males, with plans for further translocations underway to bolster their population even more.
